review_evidence: README documents a no-sorry, zero-project-axiom VJP proof suite, denotational ties to emitted StableHLO, floating-point error bridges, descent theorems and robustness certificates.

232 of 573 Lean files contain proposition declarations; LeanMlir/Proofs alone contains large theorem families for derivatives/VJPs, architectures, Float32 error analysis, SGD descent and certified render bridges.
The formal proof content is central to the repository and is independently useful formal-methods and analysis prior art despite the surrounding code-generation/training infrastructure.

summary: Surveyed all 598 listed .lean files by directory (Bestiary, LeanMlir incl. 193 under LeanMlir/Proofs, LeanMlir/Verified, apps, demos, jax, tests, historical, planning, runs, scripts), sizes at both extremes, and a declaration grep over the whole set. 587 files hold Lean declarations (defs, structures, theorems; 247 files carry theorem/lemma statements, including the verified VJP/architecture proofs and the large generated Lipschitz/IBP/SDP certificate scorecards), so they stay searchable. Eleven files have no declarations; I read each. Six are excluded: three Lake build configurations and three one-off run scripts whose only content is #eval calls writing MLIR to another machine's absolute scratch path. Retained among the declaration-free files: jax/Jax.lean (import-only aggregator, kept primary-eligible under FILTER-007), tests/AuditAxioms.lean and tests/AuditAxiomsHeavy.lean (#print axioms lists with commentary that names and describes the audited theorems), and LeanMlir/Proofs/Codegen/ChapterArtifacts.lean and MlpArtifacts.lean (in-tree artifact writers documenting which verified renderers produce the committed MLIR).
